claims.rationale: This is convergent preclinical evidence across distinct rodent models, not evidence of established human efficacy or of efficacy for an as-yet-undefined SGL-001 product.
claims.statement: Intranasal EV treatment was associated with improved inflammatory, histologic, or functional outcomes in several rodent CNS injury or disease models.

claims.rationale: The result supports investigation of a consistent source-cell strategy but does not establish a clinically acceptable manufacturing process.
claims.statement: A clonal immortalized MSC source produced EVs with activity comparable to primary MSC-EVs in one neonatal mouse hypoxic-ischemic injury study, suggesting a testable route to reduce source heterogeneity during scale-up.

claims.rationale: MISEV2023 provides an expert-consensus framework for rigorous EV characterization and functional studies; it is not a product-specific regulatory approval standard.
claims.statement: EV development requires controlled production, separation, identity and purity characterization, functional testing, and transparent reporting because EV preparations are heterogeneous and may contain non-vesicular co-isolates.

evidence.excerpt: Curated summary: repeated intranasal EV administration after hypoxic-ischemic injury reduced brain tissue atrophy in neonatal mice; EVs from a clonal immortalized MSC line and primary MSCs showed comparable effects. The study frames source-cell consistency and scale as translational considerations.
evidence.title: Extracellular vesicles from immortalized mesenchymal stromal cells protect against neonatal hypoxic-ischemic brain injury

evidence.excerpt: Curated summary: the ISEV consensus identifies continuing challenges in EV nomenclature, separation from non-vesicular particles, characterization, functional studies, production reporting, and in-vivo evaluation; it recommends transparent, orthogonal characterization and appropriate controls.
evidence.title: Minimal information for studies of extracellular vesicles (MISEV2023): From basic to advanced approaches

hypothesis.rationale: Rodent CNS-injury studies support testing intranasal delivery and biological activity as enabling evidence rather than defining the intended indication; non-human-primate evidence makes delivery translation the principal uncertainty, and MISEV2023 supports tighter product characterization.
hypothesis.statement: An intranasal MSC-derived small-EV formulation with controlled identity, purity, dose, and potency attributes can achieve reproducible CNS exposure and a neuroregeneration-relevant pharmacodynamic signal in a cognition or aging model, but advancement should be gated on quantitative biodistribution and translation-oriented acceptance criteria.
hypothesis.test_plan: Compare a characterized candidate formulation with vehicle, free-label, and disrupted-EV controls; quantify intact-EV-associated exposure across CNS, nasal, pulmonary, and systemic compartments over time; pair exposure with a predefined neuroregeneration-relevant pharmacodynamic assay, then evaluate cognitive function in an aging-relevant model only if prospectively defined exposure, reproducibility, and safety criteria are met.

matter.question: What minimum source-cell, EV identity, cargo, and release definition is required before SGL-001 can be treated as a candidate-like product?
matter.title: Candidate and product definition
matter.why_it_matters: An undefined candidate prevents interpretable formulation, biodistribution, manufacturing, and translational work.

program.current_formulation_hypothesis: Intranasal mesenchymal-stromal-cell-derived small-EV preparation with defined identity, purity, dose, and a mechanism-relevant potency assay; therapeutic cargo remains to be selected.
program.largest_unresolved_risk: Intranasal CNS exposure observed in rodents may not translate to larger species or humans.
program.name: SGL-001 development program
program.next_proposed_action: Run a formulation-controlled biodistribution and pharmacology study with label controls, quantitative tissue exposure, and predefined acceptance criteria, then select a cognition/aging model aligned with the program intent.

risks.description: EV heterogeneity, co-isolates, source-cell variability, and process changes may alter composition, dose, stability, or biological activity.
risks.mitigation: Define the source-cell strategy, scalable purification process, orthogonal identity and purity panel, stability-indicating assays, and a mechanism-linked potency assay.
risks.title: Product identity and potency may not be reproducible
